APT-ENG-0269: The error lies in segment (A) 'She prefer'. The third-person singular subject pronoun 'She' requires the singular verb 'prefers' in the simple present tense. Correct sentence: 'She prefers tea to coffee in the morning.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0270: The error lies in segment (B) 'is waiting'. The partitive phrase 'A number of + plural noun' functions as a plural quantifier and takes a plural verb ('are waiting'). APT-ENG-0271: The error lies in segment (B) 'have been selected'. The distributive pronoun 'Neither' is singular in formal grammar and takes the singular auxiliary verb 'has been selected'. APT-ENG-0272: The error lies in segment (A) 'The jury was divided'. APT-ENG-0273: The error lies in segment (C) 'since four days'. A duration or period of time ('four days') takes the preposition 'for', not 'since'. Correct sentence: 'He has been absent for four days.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0274: The error lies in segment (B) 'than all her colleagues'. Comparative adjectives ending in '-ior' (such as senior, junior, superior) take the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'She is senior to all her colleagues.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0275: The error lies in segment (B) 'the room than'. The negative adverb 'Scarcely' pairs with the conjunction 'when', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'Scarcely had I entered the room when the phone rang.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0276: The error lies in segment (B) 'many advices'. The noun 'advice' is uncountable in English and cannot be pluralized as 'advices'; it takes 'much advice' or 'many pieces of advice'. Correct sentence: 'He gave me much advice regarding my career.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0277: The error lies in segment (A) 'The police is'. The noun 'police' is a plural collective noun and takes the plural verb 'are', not 'is'. Correct sentence: 'The police are investigating the matter.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0279: The error lies in segment (B) 'when the students rushed out'. The correlative pair with 'No sooner' is 'than', not 'when'. Correct sentence: 'No sooner did the bell ring than the students rushed out.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0294: The error lies in segment (A) 'had expect'. The past perfect auxiliary 'had' requires the past participle form 'expected', not the base form 'expect'. Correct sentence: 'My students had expected guidance from my end.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0298: The error lies in segment (C) 'looking anybody'. The intransitive verb 'look' requires the preposition 'at' before an object: 'without looking at anybody'. Correct sentence: 'Deepa walked down the road slowly without looking at anybody.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0309: The error lies in segment (A) 'the most feared form'. The partitive phrase 'one of the + superlative + plural noun' requires the plural form 'forms'. Correct sentence: 'Public speaking is one of the most feared forms of communication.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0313: The error lies in segment (B) 'I goes'. The first-person subject 'I' takes the base verb 'go', not the inflected third-person singular form 'goes'. Correct sentence: 'I go to the school every day irrespective of the weather.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0314: The error lies in segment (C) 'the football'. Names of sports and games (such as football, cricket, tennis) do not take articles. Correct sentence: 'Ronaldo is a famous player of football.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0315: The error lies in segment (B) 'There is many ways'. The post-verbal subject 'many ways' is plural, requiring the plural verb 'There are', not 'There is'. Correct sentence: 'There are many ways to make a stranger feel welcome in the community.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0318: The error lies in segment (C) 'happy'. The verb 'playing' must be modified by an adverb of manner ('happily'), not an adjective ('happy'). Correct sentence: 'The children were playing happily in the garden.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0322: The error lies in segment (C) 'are very'. The noun 'scenery' is uncountable and singular, requiring the singular verb 'is', not 'are'. Correct sentence: 'The scenery of Kashmir is very enchanting.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0323: The error lies in segment (B) 'told me'. Following the auxiliary 'did not', the main verb must appear in its base form 'tell', not the past tense 'told'. Correct sentence: 'He did not tell me anything about it.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0324: The error lies in segment (B) 'than me'. The comparative adjective 'junior' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'She is junior to me in college.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0325: The error lies in segment (A) 'I have'. A specific past time adverb like 'yesterday' requires the simple past tense ('saw'), not the present perfect ('have seen'). Correct sentence: 'I saw him yesterday.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0326: The error lies in segment (B) 'has caught'. The noun 'police' is a plural collective noun requiring the plural auxiliary verb 'have caught', not 'has caught'. Correct sentence: 'The police have caught the thief.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0327: The error lies in segment (B) 'are his'. APT-ENG-0328: The error lies in segment (B) 'very fastly'. 'Fast' serves as both an adjective and an adverb in standard English; 'fastly' is non-standard. Correct sentence: 'He walked very fast to catch the train.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0329: The error lies in segment (A) 'Unless you do not apologize'. 'Unless' has an inherent negative meaning ('if not'); pairing it with 'do not' creates an erroneous double negative. Correct sentence: 'Unless you apologize, you will be punished.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0330: The error lies in segment (B) 'student'. The partitive structure 'One of the + plural noun' requires 'students'. Correct sentence: 'One of the students was absent.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0331: The error lies in segment (B) 'to do'. The adjective 'capable' takes the preposition 'of' followed by a gerund ('capable of doing'), not the infinitive 'to do'. Correct sentence: 'He is capable of doing this work.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0332: The error lies in segment (B) 'have given'. APT-ENG-0333: The error lies in segment (C) 'was present'. When subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('the students', plural), which takes 'were present'. APT-ENG-0334: The error lies in segment (A) 'in a such a'. The double indefinite article is grammatically incorrect; the proper construction is 'in such a cordial manner'. Correct sentence: 'She behaves in such a cordial manner that everyone admires her.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-0337: The error lies in segment (B) 'are fattening'. The indefinite pronoun 'Everything' is grammatically singular and requires the singular verb 'is fattening', not 'are'. Correct sentence: 'Everything that I like to eat is fattening.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
